key_insight: UGKWP local time stepping is made rigorously conservative by fixing each cell’s time step, which preserves time-averaged particle flux balance while speeding steady multiscale flow convergence.
engineering_relevance: The method can cut steady-state CFD wall-clock time substantially, making multiscale simulations around complex geometries more practical.
method: Use a fixed per-cell local time step Δt_i instead of time-varying local steps
Rescale particle mass and free-transport time at cell interfaces to maintain conservation
Apply UGKWP-LTS to steady multiscale flows under a rigorously justified flux-balance framework
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 3.8×–20× faster convergence and up to 21× lower wall-clock time versus global time stepping, validated on cylinder and flat-plate benchmarks.
watch_item: The conservation guarantee depends on keeping Δt_i fixed per cell; implementations that let local steps vary in time may lose the proven flux-balance property.
paper_title: Rigorously justified local time stepping in UGKWP method for steady multiscale flow simulation
